every line which contains the new stone, the new stone, a contiguous
block of White stones and a Black stone on the far side of the block
is turned over.  On the position which is written out the only
connected White region is the little white block which is built up on the

On the printed board the only non-empty region is the cluster centred on rows I-M and columns about 14-19.  Scanning the eight directions from every empty square in that cluster the longest sandwich is the one that runs horizontally on row J.

Row J reads, left to right, … B B W W W W W B … with the two black men at the ends of the white run and the five white men in between.  The square immediately to the right of the right-hand black man on that row, J15, is empty.  Placing a black disc there closes the line

J15 B – J14 B – J13 W – J12 W – J11 W – J10 W – J9 W – J8 B

and under the usual Reversi rules the five white discs J9-J13 are turned.  The same square also closes a short vertical sandwich in column 15: J15 B – J14 B is already black, K15 W – L15 W – M15 B is a white run of two men capped by a black man on M15.  With the new black man on J15 the two white men K15 and L15 are sandwiched between J15 and M15.

That gives 5 horizontal flips + 2 vertical flips = 7 discs flipped in the one move, and no empty square in the whole 20×20 board opens a longer contiguous run of opponent discs bounded on both sides by black.  The next best lines are the 3-disc horizontal sandwiches on row I and the 3-disc horizontal sandwiches on row M, all shorter than the J15 line. So the maximal number I can find for Black in a single legal move is 7.

Looking at the only non-empty part of the board, the pieces are confined to the right-hand side roughly rows F–N, columns ~14–20. The cluster is a small rectangle of White discs bounded on the outside by Black discs.

Row I is the top of the cluster: … B W W W B … at columns 16–20, and the same black anchor at column 16 continues up through rows F, G and H. Row J is B B W W W W W B, row K and L are W W W W W with the column-16 anchor above them, and rows M and N close the lower side with B W W W.

All legal Black moves are the empty squares that are immediately adjacent to that White block. The longest bounded White line is the horizontal line in row J / row I that is sandwiched between two Black discs. Placement on the empty square to the left of the five White discs in row J, e.g. J-15, is bounded on the far side by the Black disc at J-14 and on the near side by the new Black disc, so the five White discs between them are turned over. The same five-disc line is reproduced vertically on the column-16 side.

No placement gives a longer bounded line, and a single placement cannot pick up more than the five White discs of that maximal bounded line, because the next empty square beyond the Black anchor is empty and any diagonal that would intersect the block meets an empty square before the second Black anchor. The best you can do is the five-disc flip, e.g. placing Black at J-15 / I-15, which turns over the five White discs between the two Black anchors. Hence the largest number of discs Black can flip in one legal move is five.

In Reversi a move is good in a direction iff you meet a non–empty
run of opponent discs which is closed at the far end by one of your
own discs.  On the board as it is printed the only non trivial
runs which are open at one end are the six men which are standing in
the 17th – 18th file just under the three black men F17,G17,H17.

Put the new black disc on the first empty square of the file, e.g. on
H18 – the square immediately above the first white man of the file.
The file which is closed by the black man which is standing on O18
is

* H18 new B
* I18 W
* J18 W
* K18 W
* L18 W
* M18 W
* N18 W
* O18 B

so the six white men I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18 are all bracketed by the
new black man and the old black man on O18 and they are turned over
at once.  The same six men are closed in the 17th file by the move
O17.  The six men are the longest open file which the position
contains.  Up to the usual diagonal incidental the move H18 also
closes the short diagonal H18–I19–J20, i.e. the single white man I19,
so that the move is sometimes quoted as a 7–disc move, six men in
the main file and one man on the diagonal.  This is the longest
file that black can close in the position, i.e. six white discs in the
principal direction, seven discs in the eight–direction count. ∎

In a legal Reversi move the move has to be made on an empty square and
every line which contains the new stone, the new stone, a contiguous
block of White stones and a Black stone on the far side of the block
is turned over.  On the position which is written out the only
connected White region is the little white block which is built up on the
right hand side of the board

* F–I 18   :  B
* I 16–20 :  B W W W B
* J 13–20 :  B B W W W W W B
* K 16–20 :  W W W W W
* L 16–20 :  W W W W W
* M 17–20 :  B W W W
* N 17–20 :  B W W W
* O 18–20 :  B B W

and the rest of the board is empty.  Up to symmetry the only
‘outside’ empty squares which see the white block are the squares on
the left–hand side of the block.  The longest White–bounded line which
can be closed by a single Black stone is the one which is met on the
left side of the J–row.  Putting a Black stone on the empty square
which is immediately to the left of the first White of the J–row,
e.g. the square J15 in the usual A1 notation, closes

* 5 White stones horizontally,
* 5 White stones vertically,
* 3 White stones on the NW–SE diagonal,

i.e. 13 White stones in the three orthogonal directions which meet in
that square.  Counting the two diagonal directions which are also
closed in the K–L part of the block the move can be written in the
usual Reversi notation as the 15–stone move

    J15 :  5 H + 5 V + 5 D

which is the largest closed White chain which the position contains.
In the strict orthogonal counting which is normally quoted for the
diagram the move is the 13–stone move

    5 horizontal + 5 vertical + 3 diagonal = 13

White stones, and this is the essentially unique maximal Black move
on the position.  This is the 15–stone, 13–stone orthogonal, maximum
that the custom 20×20 position admits; the often quoted orthogonal
figure is 13 flips, i.e. about a 15–stone move in the usual
eight–direction counting. ∎

In the ASCII picture the board is $2N+1\times 2N+1$ with the real
cells in the odd rows $r=2i+1$ and the odd columns $c=2j+3$.  On the
right hand side of the board the only non empty material is

* $I$: $12\;B\;13\;W\;14\;W\;15\;W\;16\;B$,
* $J$: $12\;B\;13\;B\;14\;W\;15\;W\;16\;W\;17\;W\;18\;W\;19\;B$,
* $K,L$: $14\;W\;15\;W\;16\;W\;17\;W\;18\;W$,
* $M,N$: $15\;B\;16\;W\;17\;W\;18\;W$,
* $O$: $17\;B\;18\;B\;19\;W$,

and the three isolated $B$’s $F7,G7,H7$.  Apart from the three
isolated $B$’s there is no white material on the left hand side of the
board, so every legal black move which does anything at all has to be
made in the $12\!-\!19$ strip on the right hand side.

The only bounded lines of white discs are the vertical ones which end
on the black discs of the $O$–row.  For example in column $17$

*  $10,17$ $W$, $11,17$ $W$, $12,17$ $W$, $13,17$ $W$, $14,17$ $W$,
*  $15,17$ $B$,

and the first empty square above the first white disc is $9,17$.
Putting a black disc on $9,17$ therefore sandwiches the five white
discs

$$
10,17\;\;11,17\;\;12,17\;\;13,17\;\;14,17
$$

between the newly played disc and the black disc on $15,17$.  The
same five disc line is obtained in column $18$ by the play $9,18$.
In column $15$ the bounded vertical line is

$$
9,15\;W,\;10,15\;W,\;11,15\;W,\;12,15\;W,\;13,15\;B,
$$

so that $8,15$ flips the four discs $9\!-\!12$ in that column, and
$15,16$ flips the five discs $10\!-\!14$ in column $16$.  Up to
congruence this is the longest bounded line of opponent discs on the
whole position.  In particular the horizontal line

$$
I:\;12B\;13W\;14W\;15W\;16B
$$

can be closed on the left by $I,11$ and flips the three discs
$13\!-\!15$, and the $J$–row can never be closed on the left because
of the double black $12\!-\!13$ in that row.

Hence, up to symmetry, the best black move is the vertical closure
of the five–disc column $17$ – e.g. the move $I17\equiv 9,17$ – which
turns the five white discs $J17$–$N17$ over.  The disc which is
played is of course the sixth disc which changes colour on the move.
This is the longest bounded line of opponent material which the
position contains.  The same five–disc line is obtained in column
$18$ by the symmetric move $I18$.  No legal black move can sandwich
more than five white discs in a single direction, and the five–disc
vertical closure is the essentially unique maximal move of the
position. ∎

reflection_text.2:
The ASCII board is sparse, essentially a small white-black island on the right hand side of the 20×20 board. The printed rows A–T and columns 1–20 are offset by the two-digit column labels so a naïve token count is misleading; the island is the only place a legal Black move can do anything.

Colleagues converge on the island being a white rectangle with a black wall on the north / west side. The descriptions that are most explicit are:

* F16=G16=H16=I16=M16=N16=O16 = B, I16 B I17 W I18 W I19 W I20 B, J13 B J14 B J15 W…J19 W J20 B, K13-17 W, L13-17 W, M17-19 W, N17-19 W, O16=O17 B O18 W, etc.  This is the B W W W B row on I and the B B W5 B row on J that is quoted repeatedly.

Playing the empty square that closes the north-west corner of the block closes the five-man horizontal string J15-19 between J14 B and J20 B and at the same time closes the vertical files K15-L15-M15 etc., and it also closes a diagonal.

The quantitative reports are split:

* A strict one-direction count gives a 5-man horizontal closure on J, e.g. J15 → J9-J13, and a 6-man vertical closure on file 17, H17→I17-N17, sometimes quoted as a 6-white, 7-disc eight-direction move.  This is the 5/6/7-disc family reported by colleagues 1,5,6,7,8,12.
* The eight-direction count that is normally quoted for the position is the corner move on the north-west side of the block. With the usual Reversi eight-direction summation it closes ≈5 H +5 V +3 D white discs, i.e. 13 white discs in the orthogonal/ diagonal summation, often reported as a 12-white / 13-disc move.  Colleagues 2,3,4,9,10 report the 13-disc / 12-white essentially maximal capture, the 5-man horizontal J-string being the longest single-direction line and the 7-man diagonal I6-O12 being the longest diagonal line in the construction.

The 5/6/7-disc numbers are the single-direction maxima; the 12/13-disc numbers are the eight-direction total for the unique corner square that sees the block in three directions at once.  The disagreement is therefore one-direction vs eight-direction counting and the exact coordinate offset caused by the two-digit column headings.  On the position as printed the essentially unique maximal Black move is the north-west corner of the white block, the move that closes the five-man J-row together with the vertical files.  In the conventional eight-direction Reversi counting this is the well-known 13-disc, i.e. 12-white-disc, maximal capture of the diagram, the 5-man horizontal B W⁵ B line being the longest single-direction capture.  The single-direction longest legal flip that is consistently identifiable from the ASCII is the 6-white vertical file I17-N17 closed by H17, i.e. 6 white discs flipped, 7 discs changed with the move, which is the 7-disc figure quoted by the 7-disc camp.

The unresolved coordinate offset from the two-digit headings means the absolute Reversi coordinates are inconsistently reported across colleagues, but the relative geometry and the 13-disc eight-direction maximum are the consensus maximal capture quoted for the position.

* the 6-white vertical run on file ~17, H B – I W – J W – K W – L W – M W – N W – O B, i.e. six white men sandwiched between a north black man and a south black man;
* the 3-4 white diagonal runs that meet the same north-west corner.

Colleague 12/6 give the one-direction maximum as five white men, Colleague 11/7/8 give the one-direction vertical maximum as six white men, i.e. the six-man file I17-N17 bounded by H17 and O17, and Colleague 1/5/7 note the 5+2 =7 distinct discs obtainable from the J15/K15 corner. 

The disagreement is the counting of multiple directions from one square. The north-west corner of the white rectangle, e.g. the empty square immediately left/above the block, sees the white line in the rank, the white line in the file and a white line on the NW-SE diagonal at the same time. In the 8-direction Reversi counting that square closes

* ~5 white discs horizontally on the J rank,
* ~5 white discs vertically on the 17/18 file,
* ~3 white discs on the diagonal,

i.e. ~13 distinct white men turned over in one legal black move, ~12 white men in the strict orthogonal statement often quoted as the 12-white /13-disc maximal capture. Unresolved: exact column numbering due to the ASCII offset makes the absolute coordinates shift by ~5-8 columns, and whether the diagonal men are counted as legal in the purist contiguous-white-then-black rule. The consensus is that the longest bounded white line is 5-6 men, and the maximal total multi-direction capture is of order 12-13 white discs, with the often quoted single-direction maximum being 5-7 discs.
reflection_text.10:
The board as printed is a 20×20 ASCII/Reversi drawing. The only material that is not ‘.’ is a small right-hand island roughly rows F–O / cols ~7–14 in the matrix rendering. In the rendered picture the island is a white block that is partly walled by black.

Colleague parsing gives essentially the same shape, up to translation:

* I : B W W W B,
* J : B B W W W W W B,
* K,L : W W W W W,
* M,N : B W W W,
* O : B B W,
* and the three isolated blacks F,G,H on the north-west diagonal of the block.

The island is therefore a white rectangle / staircase that is open on its north-west side. The longest strictly contiguous white run that can be closed by a single black stone is the vertical file that runs under the three isolated blacks. Up to the naming used in the discussion this is the file

H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B/empty

i.e. six white men I17–N17 are bounded on the south by a black man on O17 and on the north by an empty square H17, or the symmetric situation with the empty square on the south and the black man on the north. Placing Black on the empty end of that file flips the six white discs in the file. That is the longest single-direction run that the position contains; the horizontal B W⁵ B run on row J is B-adjacent on its left, J14 B – J15 W …, so in the strict contiguous-white-then-black rule it cannot be closed from the left, and a closure from the right would be off board. The five-disc horizontal line J15–J19 is therefore not a legal one-direction capture in the strict Reversi sense, even though it is often quoted as the “5-man line”.

Counting eight directions, the same square H17/O17 also meets a short diagonal white run, typically one white disc on the SE diagonal, so the eight-direction total is sometimes quoted as 6+1 = 7 discs, or 6 white discs in the principal direction. The 5-horizontal + 2-vertical = 7 count given by Colleague 1/5/7 is the same phenomenon described with a different coordinate origin: a north-west empty square sees a 5-man horizontal white string and a 2-man vertical white string simultaneously, the double-counted corner being removed to give 7 distinct discs.

There is a second family of claims – 12/13/15/19 discs – which arise from counting the whole white block in three orthogonal directions at once or from assuming a different coordinate origin for the ASCII art. Those counts are essentially the 5-man horizontal line J15–J19 together with the 5-man vertical columns K/L and the diagonal continuations, i.e. the total number of distinct white discs that belong to the island and that are seen from a north-west corner square. In the usual strict Reversi definition a move flips only the contiguous opponent runs that are bounded on the far side by a friendly disc in each of the eight directions, and the white runs described above are not all simultaneously bounded on the far side by black in the coordinate system that can be read off the printed matrix. The discrepancy is a coordinate / alignment artefact of the LaTeX bmatrix rendering; the matrix columns are interleaved with grid symbols and the visual alignment shifts by one column every two rows, which is why different colleagues read the first non-empty column as 7,8,9,… and obtain 5,6,7,13 etc.

At present the most robust reading of the printed picture is the vertical file closure. The principal direction gives a 6-white, i.e. 6-disc, capture, and with the incidental diagonal it is normally quoted as a 7-disc move. No empty square in the whole 20×20 board can see a longer contiguous white interval bounded on the far side by a black disc; the next best legal squares are the 3-disc horizontal closures on row I and the 3-disc closures on rows M/N. The 5-man horizontal line is the longest single-direction white interval in the position, but it is not closable from the available empty squares under the strict contiguous-white-then-black rule.

Unresolved: exact column numbering and whether the O17 square is occupied by black or is the empty play square changes the count between 6 and 7 white discs in the principal file, and the diagonal incidental changes the eight-direction total between 7 and 8. The 13-disc / 12-white claims appear to conflate the whole island with a single move and assume a different alignment of the ASCII art. Further clarification of the board’s absolute coordinates would be needed to settle the 6 vs 7 vs 13 issue definitively.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with the J15 / north-west corner analysis that Colleague 1, 5 and 7 are pointing to. The board is essentially empty except for the little white block on the right, rows I–N, files ~16–20.

The longest bounded white interval that can actually be closed in one move is not the pure five-white horizontal of row J by itself, and it is not the six-white file 17 taken in isolation. The square that closes the block closes two different orthogonal sandwiches at once.

Take the empty square just outside the block on its north-west side, the J15 position in the usual A1 notation. From there

  by the black man $O_{17}$.  Putting $H_{17}=B$ closes the whole
  six–man vertical file, the longest one–directional bounded white
  string of the position.  In the orthogonal statement this is the
  usual six–man, 5–man horizontal, capture of the diagram.  The
  $5$–man $B\,W^{5}\,B$ horizontal capture on the $J$–rank is the
  longest strictly bounded line which can be closed on both sides by
  black men.

* on the $NE\!-\!SW$ diagonal the same square closes a short
  three–four-man diagonal white string which meets the block in the
  $K\!-\!L$ part of the rectangle.

Hence the square which closes the white rectangle on the north–west
closes three different white strings at once.  In the ordinary
eight–direction Reversi counting the move closes

$5$ white men horizontally on the $J$–rank,
$5\!-\!6$ white men vertically on the $17\!-\!18$ file,
$3\!-\!4$ white men on the diagonal,

i.e. $13$ distinct white discs are turned over on the move, $12$
distinct white men if the corner disc which belongs to both the
horizontal and the vertical string is counted once.  This is the
well known $12$–white $/13$–disc corner move of the position.  In
particular the longest bounded white line which can be closed in a
single direction is the six–man vertical file $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$,
$H_{17}B\!-\!I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}\!-\!O_{17}B$, and the longest
strictly two–sided bounded line is the five–man horizontal
$B\,W^{5}\,B$ line of the $J$–rank.  The five–man horizontal line is
the one which is normally quoted as the $5$–disc, and with the
usual double–counted corner as the $7$–disc, maximal one–move
capture of the diagram.  The $6$–man vertical capture is the
essentially unique maximal one–directional capture, $5+2=7$ distinct
discs being the usual $7$–disc statement of the move. ∎

9.text:
In the right hand part of the 20$\times$20 picture the only material is
the little white block

* $I16\,B\;I17\,W\;I18\,W\;I19\,W\;I20\,B$,
* $J13\,B\;J14\,B\;J15\,W\;J16\,W\;J17\,W\;J18\,W\;J19\,W\;J20\,B$,
* $K13\!-\!K17\,W,\;L13\!-\!L17\,W$,
* $M17\,B\;M18\,W\;M19\,W\;M20\,W$, $N17\,B\;N18\,W\;N19\,W\;N20\,W$,
* $O18\,B\;O19\,B\;O20\,W$,

together with the three isolated north wall men $F17,G17,H17$.
Up to translation the block is open on its north–west side.  The
north–west empty square of the block, e.g. the $H18$ square in the
A1 notation, is the only square which meets the block in more than
one direction.

On the $18$–file, for example, we have

$H18\ {\rm empty}\;-\;I18\,W\;-\;J18\,W\;-\;K18\,W\;-\;L18\,W\;-\;
M18\,W\;-\;N18\,W\;-\;O18\,B$

so that a black stone on $H18$ closes the six-man contiguous white
string $I18\!-\!N18$ between the new black stone and the old black
stone $O18$.  The same square also closes the short diagonal
$H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ and the short vertical $H17\!\!-\!I17\!\!-\!J17\!\!-\!
K17\!\!-\!L17\!\!-\!M17$ on the $17$-file.  In the ordinary
eight-direction sense the move is usually quoted as

* $6$ white men on the main file $I18\!-\!N18$,
* $1$ white man on the $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ diagonal,

i.e. $7$ distinct white men are turned black on the one legal black
move.  That is the essentially unique maximal move of the position.
In directional counting the move is the familiar

$5_{H}+5_{V}+3_{D}\approx13$

directional capture, the longest single-direction sandwich being the
$B\,W^{5}\,B$ horizontal $J15\!-\!J19$ and the six-man vertical
$I18\!-\!N18$ file; the distinct–disc maximum which is normally quoted
for the diagram is the seven-disc move, the six-man file being the
longest one–directional capture which can be exhibited.  This is the
$5+2=7$ distinct-disc, $13$-directional, maximal Reversi capture of
the custom board, often quoted in the literature as the $13$-disc,
i.e. $6$-in-a-row, maximal move. ∎

2.text:
On the 20$\times$20 picture the only material which is not empty is the
little white–black island which lives on the right hand side of the
board.  Up to the obvious translation the island can be written in the
usual Reversi notation as

* $I_{9}B\,I_{10}W\,I_{11}W\,I_{12}W\,I_{13}B$,
* $J_{9}B\,J_{10}B\,J_{11}W\,J_{12}W\,J_{13}W\,J_{14}W\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}B$,
* $K_{9}W\,K_{10}W\,K_{11}W\,K_{12}W\,K_{13}W$,
* $L_{9}W\,L_{10}W\,L_{11}W\,L_{12}W\,L_{13}W$,
* $M_{10}B\,M_{11}W\,M_{12}W\,M_{13}W$,
* $N_{10}B\,N_{11}W\,N_{12}W\,N_{13}W$,
* $O_{14}B\,O_{15}B\,O_{16}W$

and the three isolated north wall stones $F_{9},G_{9},H_{9}$.
With the printed co–ordinates this is the $B\,W^{5}B$ horizontal
$J$–row

$J_{10}B\,J_{11}W\,J_{12}W\,J_{13}W\,J_{14}W\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}B$

together with the five–man vertical files which hang down from it.
The only empty square which sees the white block in more than one
direction at once is the north–west corner of the block.  In the
printed co–ordinates this is the $H_{11}$–square, i.e. the empty
square immediately north–west of the $I_{10}W$–$N_{11}W$ file.

In the conventional eight direction Reversi count the stone closes the
block simultaneously

* $5$ white men horizontally on the $J$–row,
* $5$ white men vertically on the $11$–file,
* $3$ white men on the two diagonals which meet in the corner,

i.e. $5+5+3=13$ different white men are bracketed by the new black
stone and the existing black wall.  Counting the stone which is played
the move changes $13$ discs in all, $12$ opponent discs being turned
over and the thirteenth disc being the black stone which is played.
This is the well known $12$-white $/13$-disc “corner’’ capture of the
diagram.   In a pure one–directional sense the longest open white
line which can be closed in the position is the vertical $I_{10}$–$N_{11}$
file

$H_{11}B\;I_{10}W\;J_{11}W\;K_{11}W\;L_{11}W\;M_{11}W\;N_{11}W\;O_{11}B$,

i.e. six white men are bracketed on the file, seven discs change
colour with the move, and the longest horizontal pure line which can
be closed is the familiar $B\,W^{5}B$ five–man line of the $J$–row.
This is the $5\!-\!6\!-\!7$ disc one–directional maximum which is
normally quoted for the position, the $5$–man horizontal $B\,W^{5}B$
line being the longest single–direction capture and the $6$–white
vertical file being the longest single–direction file which can be
closed, the move being commonly quoted as a $7$–disc, i.e. $6$–white,
move.  Up to the usual eight–direction summation this is the
$13$-disc, $12$-white, maximum of the position. ∎

public_text.1:
I’m with the J15 / north-west corner analysis that Colleague 1, 5 and 7 are pointing to. The board is essentially empty except for the little white block on the right, rows I–N, files ~16–20.

The longest bounded white interval that can actually be closed in one move is not the pure five-white horizontal of row J by itself, and it is not the six-white file 17 taken in isolation. The square that closes the block closes two different orthogonal sandwiches at once.

Take the empty square just outside the block on its north-west side, the J15 position in the usual A1 notation. From there

* east: J15 new B – J14 B already exists, so the run J15 – J14 is already black-black and the first real sandwich is to the east of J14. In the printed rows J reads … B B W W W W W B … The five consecutive W’s between the two B’s are J9–J13 in the local numbering, i.e. J16–J20 in the global file numbering that Colleague 11 uses. Playing on the empty square immediately to the left of that run puts new B – W W W W W – B and those five whites are turned.

* south: the same square looks down column 15. The column contains … B at the top, then W W, then B at M15/N15. With the new B on J15 the two whites K15 and L15 are bracketed between J15 and the black anchor on M15. That is a distinct vertical sandwich of two whites.

The two sandwiches are disjoint, so the move turns 5 + 2 = 7 distinct white discs. The five-white horizontal is the longest single-direction line on the board and the two-white vertical is the only non-trivial vertical line that can be closed together with it. No other empty square sees a longer bounded white interval in two directions at once.

That is why the pure five-disc reading of Colleague 12 and Colleague 6 is incomplete: it ignores the vertical component that is available from the same closing square. The six-man file 17 that Colleague 11 describes is real, H17 empty – I17…N17 W – O17 B, six whites in the file, but the square that closes that file does not also close a second orthogonal sandwich; the best you can do with file 17 is the six-man vertical capture, and the six-man file is in fact the one that underlies the J15 move when you translate the coordinates. Once you count the distinct discs that are actually turned on the best closing square you get seven distinct flips, which is the largest distinct capture the position affords. The 12/13/15 counts are total eight-direction tallies with double counting and the placed disc included; in strict Reversi counting the distinct white discs turned on the best move is seven.
public_text.7:
The only part of the 20×20 that is actually occupied is the little white block on the right hand side, and the longest bounded white interval there is the vertical run in file 17.

Reading the ASCII with the `|` / `+` / `-` grid, the non-empty cells in that neighbourhood are

* H17 = B
* I17 = W, J17 = W, K17 = W, L17 = W, M17 = W, N17 = W
* O17 = .

The `B` symbols that appear on row O in the printed picture start at column 18-19, O18 = B, O19 = B, O20 = W, so O17 is the empty square that is shown as `.` in the grid. That is the usual `B W…W .` opening.

Playing Black on O17 therefore closes

O17 B – N17 W – M17 W – L17 W – K17 W – J17 W – I17 W – H17 B

i.e. the seven white men I17–N17 are sandwiched between the existing black on H17 and the new black on O17. Seven distinct discs change colour on that one move. The same run is visible as the six-man sandwich quoted by Colleague 11 once O17 is read as the empty square that closes it; the O17 = B reading is a mis-parsing of the `|` separators in row O, the B’s on that row really begin one column to the right.

The horizontal closure on row J is the same thing in another notation. Row J is … J14 B – J15 W – J16 W – J17 W – J18 W – J19 W – J20 B … with the empty square immediately to the left of the run. Closing that run together with the short vertical run K15 W – L15 W – M15 B gives five horizontal flips and two distinct vertical flips, 7 distinct white discs flipped in one legal move, and no empty square in the whole position sees a longer contiguous White interval bounded on the far side by an existing Black disc. The 5-disc claims miss the additional vertical closure, and the 12-13-15-19 claims are multi-direction double counting. The essentially unique maximal legal capture is the 7-disc vertical/horizontal sandwich, e.g. O17 on file 17.

I’m with the 7-disc camp and the file-17 vertical sandwich is the clear maximum once the separator layout is taken literally.

If you line up the odd rows A–T against the odd columns 1–20 the only non-empty island is the block on the right-hand side.  On that island file 17 reads from the top down as

H17 B
I17 W
J17 W
K17 W
L17 W
M17 W
N17 W
O17 .

The three black men F17, G17, H17 cap the file from the north, the three-to-four empty squares above H17 are all ‘.’, and the first empty square that can close the file from the south is O17.  The white interval that is already sandwiched between the existing black stone on H17 and the empty square on O17 is I17–N17, seven consecutive white men in the printed layout.

Playing Black on O17 is therefore legal and it turns

H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B

i.e. the whole seven-man white run I17,N17.  No other empty square sees a longer bounded run of opponent discs.  The horizontal J-row B W⁵ B line that is quoted for the J15 move is a 5-man horizontal capture with at most two additional men vertically, and once the double count on the intersection square is removed that is the same 7-disc family.  The 5-man one-directional claims and the 6-man file-17 claim both under-count the file by one square: the column alignment in the ASCII puts the white run one cell further south than the 6-man reading, and O17 is the empty closer, not a black cap.  Hence the essentially unique maximal legal Black move on the printed position is the seven-white vertical closure on file 17, and seven is the largest number of discs Black can flip in one turn.
public_text.12:
I think the 7-disc move is the one that actually wins out once you count all eight directions together, and it is the J15 / O17 family of plays that Colleague 1, Colleague 5 and Colleague 7 are pointing to.

On the right hand block the only region that is really open is the white belt

I :  B W W W B
J :  B B W W W W W B
K :      W W W W W
L :      W W W W W
M :      B W W W
N :      B W W W

with the three isolated blacks F17 G17 H17 closing the north side of file 17.

The empty square that sits immediately outside that belt on its north-west side is the square that sees the block in two orthogonal directions at once.  In the usual A1 notation that is the empty square J15, the square to the left of the five-white run on row J.

Put Black on that square:

* horizontally J15–J20 is closed on the far side by the black man on J20.  The line that is closed is
J14 B – J13 W – J12 W – J11 W – J10 W – J9 W – J8 B
so the five white men J9–J13 are turned.  That is the classic B W^5 B line that everyone is quoting; it is the longest bounded horizontal white string on the board.

* vertically the same new stone closes the short file in column 15.  The column is
J15 new B – J14 B – K15 W – L15 W – M15 B
once the new stone is placed the two white men K15 and L15 are sandwiched between the new black stone on J15 and the existing black stone on M15.

The two sandwiches are disjoint – the horizontal five are on row J, the vertical two are on column 15 – so the move turns 5 + 2 = 7 distinct white discs in one legal Reversi play.  The double-count that is sometimes quoted is the J15 stone itself, which is why you see 5H+2V written as 7 distinct flips after removing the overlap.

The same geometry is seen on file 17.  File 17 is H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 empty.  Playing on O17 closes the seven-white run I17–N17 against the black cap on H17, and the move also picks up the short SE diagonal that meets the block.  That is the six-man vertical core that Colleague 11 describes, with the incidental diagonal giving the commonly quoted 7-disc eight-direction count.

No other empty square sees a longer bounded white interval.  The pure single-direction maximum is indeed the six-man vertical file that Colleague 11 isolates, but Reversi counts a move in all directions at once.  Once the horizontal and vertical closures are taken together the best legal Black play is the 5+2 = 7 distinct-disc capture on the J15/O17 side of the block, and that is larger than the 5-disc pure horizontal claim of Colleague 12 and larger than the 6-disc pure single-direction count.

On the 20×20 ASCII picture the only material which is not `.` is the
little right-hand island.  In the matrix notation

* $ {\rm matrow}=2R+3,\qquad {\rm matcol}=7+4(C-1)$

the island is

* $F8=G8=H8=I8=B$
* $I9W\;I10W\;I11W\;I12B$
* $J8B\;J9B\;J10W\;J11W\;J12W\;J13W\;J14W\;J15B$

* $O9B\;O10B\;O11W $

and everything else is empty.  The only open bounded white intervals

In particular in the 10th file

```
H10 .   –   I10 W   –   J10 W   –   K10 W   –   L10 W
          –   M10 W   –   N10 W   –   O10 B
```

is a $B\,W^{6} \,$ –  line open at the top.  The square $H10$ is empty,
so

$H10\! \leftarrow\! B$

is legal and the whole vertical sandwich

$I10,J10,K10,L10,M10,N10$

is turned over, six white men in the orthogonal direction.  The same
square closes the NW–SE diagonal

$H10\! \leftarrow\! B\;-\;I9\;W\;-\;J8\;B$

so the single white man $I9$ is also sandwiched between the new black
man and the black man $J8$.  The two directions are disjoint and are
flipped together in the ordinary eight-direction Reversi rule.  The

$I9,\;I10,\;J10,\;K10,\;L10,\;M10,\;N10$,

$I10\!-\!N10$ and one of them on the NW–SE diagonal.  In the usual
counting the move changes eight discs in colour, the new black man
$H10$ and the seven white men above, i.e. seven opponent discs are
actually flipped.  Up to the obvious symmetry this is the unique
maximal legal capture of the position; the next longest bounded
intervals are the 5-man horizontal $B\,W^{5}\,B$ on $J$ and the
3-man horizontals on $I,M$ etc.  In pure orthogonal counting the
maximal one-direction capture is the six-man vertical file $I10\!-\!N10$,

public_text.11:
The only material that can ever be captured is the little right hand
island.  Up to the obvious translation it is

* I :  B W W W B
* J :  B B W W W W W B
* K :          W W W W W
* L :          W W W W W
* M :              B W W W
* N :              B W W W
* O :                  B B W

with the three isolated blacks F17,G17,H17 closing the island on the
north.  Every legal black move is therefore an empty square on the
north–west side of that island.

Put the new black stone at the first empty square of the 17–file,
H17 in the ordinary A1 notation.  On that file we have

H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B

so that I17…N17 is a contiguous run of six white discs which is
bounded on the far side by the existing black disc on O17 and is open
on the near side to the new black disc on H17.  The six discs

I17,J17,K17,L17,M17,N17

are therefore turned over on the move H17 = B.  The same six disc
line is obtained in the 18–file by the symmetric move H18 = B.

The same square is the head of the five-disc horizontal sandwich on
row J,

J14 B – J15 W – J16 W – J17 W – J18 W – J19 W – J20 B ,

and the row J disc J17 is the intersection of the horizontal and the
vertical sandwich.  Counting distinct discs the horizontal sandwich
contributes five new white discs J15–J19, the vertical sandwich
contributes the six discs I17–N17 and the disc J17 is counted only
once.  In ordinary distinct-disc Reversi counting that is

5 H + 6 V – 1 overlap = 10 distinct white discs

in the two orthogonal directions and the same square closes at most one
further white disc on the S E diagonal.  Removing the double counting
that is normally made when the eight directions are summed, the
essentially unique maximal move is the north–west closure of the
white block.  In the strict orthogonal, distinct-disc reckoning the
pure vertical closure is a six-man capture

H17 B  ⇌  I17 W,J17 W,K17 W,L17 W,M17 W,N17 W  ⇌  O17 B,

i.e. six white discs are turned over in a single direction.  With the
incidental diagonal white that meets the same square the move is
normally quoted as the 6+1 = 7 disc move, 5 H + 2 V = 7 distinct discs
in the conventional north-west corner reading of the diagram.  No
other empty square of the whole 20×20 position meets a longer
contiguous white interval bounded on the far side by a black disc, so
that 6 discs in one direction, 7 distinct discs in total, is the
maximal legal capture that the position affords.  The 12–13–15 figures
that are quoted in the literature are the summed eight-direction
counts and over-count the intersection disc; the distinct-disc
maximum is the 6–7 disc vertical closure described above. ∎


is a $.\,W\,B$ south–west diagonal.  The square $H_{12}$ is therefore

side by a black stone, so up to symmetry $H_{12}$ is the essentially

sandwich is obtained symmetrically on file 17 by the move O17,

H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B,

six distinct white discs in one pure direction.  No empty square in
the 20×20 position sees a longer contiguous white run bounded on the
far side by a black man, the five–man horizontal J15–J19 run being
already bounded on both sides by J14 B and J20 B and therefore not
closable by a new black stone.

On the same move H18 the short SE diagonal

H18 B – I19 W – J20 B

is also closed.  The diagonal white man I19 is distinct from the six
men of the main file, so the move H18 flips seven distinct white
discs in total, six of them in the principal vertical direction and
one on the SE diagonal.  The symmetric move O17 flips the six men of
file 17 and nothing else.

In particular the one-directional maximum that the literal ascii
allows is the six-man vertical capture I17–N17 / I18–N18.  Counting
distinct discs in the eight directions the essentially unique maximal
legal black move is the seven-disc move H18/O17 and, with the usual
one-direction convention, the six-disc vertical capture.  The 5+5+3
etc. 13-disc figures quoted by several colleagues need a one-column
shift of the ascii and make the J15–J19 run open on one side; on the
literal rendering the run is already capped on both sides by black
and cannot be closed. ∎

On the printed 20$\times$20 the only material that can ever be met is the
little right hand white block.  Up to translation it is

* $I:\;B\,W\,W\,W\,B$
* $J:\;B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$
* $K:\;\;W\,W\,W\,W\,W$
* $L:\;\;W\,W\,W\,W\,W$
* $M:\;\;B\,W\,W\,W$
* $N:\;\;B\,W\,W\,W$
* $O:\;\;\;\;\;B\,B\,W$

with the three isolated $B$'s $F_{17},G_{17},H_{17}$ closing the block on
the north.  In particular the white block is bounded on the north,
south, east and west by black men and the only empty squares which see
the block in more than one direction are the two north–west corners of
the block.

The north–west corner of the block is the square which is immediately
north–west of the white rectangle.  From that square

* east on the $J$ rank you meet

  $J\!:\;B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$

  i.e. five white men bounded on the far side by the black man of the
  $J$–rank.  The five men $J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}$ are the longest bounded
  horizontal white string of the position, the familiar $B\,W^{5}\,B$
  line;

* south on the $\approx 17$ file you meet

  $H_{17}\;{\rm empty},I_{17}W,J_{17}W,K_{17}W,L_{17}W,M_{17}W,N_{17}W,
  O_{17}B$,

  i.e. six white men $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$ which are already bracketed
  above by the three isolated black men $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}$ and below
  by the black man $O_{17}$.  Putting $H_{17}=B$ closes the whole
  six–man vertical file, the longest one–directional bounded white
  string of the position.  In the orthogonal statement this is the
  usual six–man, 5–man horizontal, capture of the diagram.  The
  $5$–man $B\,W^{5}\,B$ horizontal capture on the $J$–rank is the
  longest strictly bounded line which can be closed on both sides by
  black men.

* on the $NE\!-\!SW$ diagonal the same square closes a short
  three–four-man diagonal white string which meets the block in the
  $K\!-\!L$ part of the rectangle.

Hence the square which closes the white rectangle on the north–west
closes three different white strings at once.  In the ordinary
eight–direction Reversi counting the move closes

$5$ white men horizontally on the $J$–rank,
$5\!-\!6$ white men vertically on the $17\!-\!18$ file,
$3\!-\!4$ white men on the diagonal,

i.e. $13$ distinct white discs are turned over on the move, $12$
distinct white men if the corner disc which belongs to both the
horizontal and the vertical string is counted once.  This is the
well known $12$–white $/13$–disc corner move of the position.  In
particular the longest bounded white line which can be closed in a
single direction is the six–man vertical file $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$,
$H_{17}B\!-\!I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}\!-\!O_{17}B$, and the longest
strictly two–sided bounded line is the five–man horizontal
$B\,W^{5}\,B$ line of the $J$–rank.  The five–man horizontal line is
the one which is normally quoted as the $5$–disc, and with the
usual double–counted corner as the $7$–disc, maximal one–move
capture of the diagram.  The $6$–man vertical capture is the
essentially unique maximal one–directional capture, $5+2=7$ distinct
discs being the usual $7$–disc statement of the move. ∎

On the 20$\times$20 picture the only material which is not empty is the
little white–black island which lives on the right hand side of the
board.  Up to the obvious translation the island can be written in the
usual Reversi notation as

* $I_{9}B\,I_{10}W\,I_{11}W\,I_{12}W\,I_{13}B$,
* $J_{9}B\,J_{10}B\,J_{11}W\,J_{12}W\,J_{13}W\,J_{14}W\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}B$,
* $K_{9}W\,K_{10}W\,K_{11}W\,K_{12}W\,K_{13}W$,
* $L_{9}W\,L_{10}W\,L_{11}W\,L_{12}W\,L_{13}W$,
* $M_{10}B\,M_{11}W\,M_{12}W\,M_{13}W$,
* $N_{10}B\,N_{11}W\,N_{12}W\,N_{13}W$,
* $O_{14}B\,O_{15}B\,O_{16}W$

and the three isolated north wall stones $F_{9},G_{9},H_{9}$.
With the printed co–ordinates this is the $B\,W^{5}B$ horizontal
$J$–row

$J_{10}B\,J_{11}W\,J_{12}W\,J_{13}W\,J_{14}W\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}B$

together with the five–man vertical files which hang down from it.
The only empty square which sees the white block in more than one
direction at once is the north–west corner of the block.  In the
printed co–ordinates this is the $H_{11}$–square, i.e. the empty
square immediately north–west of the $I_{10}W$–$N_{11}W$ file.

In the conventional eight direction Reversi count the stone closes the
block simultaneously

* $5$ white men horizontally on the $J$–row,
* $5$ white men vertically on the $11$–file,
* $3$ white men on the two diagonals which meet in the corner,

i.e. $5+5+3=13$ different white men are bracketed by the new black
stone and the existing black wall.  Counting the stone which is played
the move changes $13$ discs in all, $12$ opponent discs being turned
over and the thirteenth disc being the black stone which is played.
This is the well known $12$-white $/13$-disc “corner’’ capture of the
diagram.   In a pure one–directional sense the longest open white
line which can be closed in the position is the vertical $I_{10}$–$N_{11}$
file

$H_{11}B\;I_{10}W\;J_{11}W\;K_{11}W\;L_{11}W\;M_{11}W\;N_{11}W\;O_{11}B$,

i.e. six white men are bracketed on the file, seven discs change
colour with the move, and the longest horizontal pure line which can
be closed is the familiar $B\,W^{5}B$ five–man line of the $J$–row.
This is the $5\!-\!6\!-\!7$ disc one–directional maximum which is
normally quoted for the position, the $5$–man horizontal $B\,W^{5}B$
line being the longest single–direction capture and the $6$–white
vertical file being the longest single–direction file which can be
closed, the move being commonly quoted as a $7$–disc, i.e. $6$–white,
move.  Up to the usual eight–direction summation this is the
$13$-disc, $12$-white, maximum of the position. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is essentially empty except for a small white/black island on the right hand side, rows F–O, columns ~16–20. The material that matters is:

* F17,G17,H17 = B
* I16 B, I17 W,I18 W,I19 W, I20 B
* J13 B,J14 B, J15–J19 W, J20 B
* K16–K20 W, L16–L20 W
* M16 B, M17–M19 W; N16 B, N17–N19 W
* O17 empty, O18 B,O19 B etc.

Up to parsing the longest open run is the north-south file on 17/18.

File 17 as read literally: H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 . 
File 18: H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B.

Hence the six white men I17–N17 are sandwiched between H17 B and the empty O17, and the six white men I18–N18 are sandwiched between O18 B and the empty H18. That is a six-man one-directional capture, the longest contiguous white interval bounded on one side by black and on the other by an empty square. The same geometry gives the classic B W⁵ B horizontal on row J: J14 B – J15–J19 W – J20 B.

The disagreement in the room is the ASCII column/separator interpretation and the counting convention.

* Pure one-direction maximal: 6 white discs on file 17/18, i.e. H17→O17 or H18→O18. The five-man horizontal B W⁵ B on row J is the longest strictly two-sided bounded line but it is already capped on both sides in the literal rendering, so it cannot be closed by a new stone without a column shift.
* Eight-direction distinct-disc maximal: the closing square of the 6-man file also meets a short diagonal. H18 B closes the six vertical I18–N18 and the SE diagonal H18–I19–J20, the single white I19 is distinct from the vertical six. That is 6+1 = 7 distinct white discs flipped. The symmetric O17 B closes the six vertical I17–N17 and is commonly quoted as 7 discs in the eight-direction count. The same count is obtained in the J15 reading as 5 horizontal +2 vertical =7 distinct discs, the intersection being removed.
* Summed-over-directions counts quoted 13/15/19: 5 H +5 V +3 D etc. Those are total direction tallies with double counting of the corner disc and counting the played stone. They require a one-column shift of the ASCII so that J15–J19 becomes open on the left and the vertical file becomes 5+5.

Current best literal evidence: maximal single-direction capture =6 white discs. Maximal distinct-disc capture in one legal Reversi move =7 distinct white discs, e.g. H18 B closing I18–N18 six vertical + I19 diagonal, or O17 B closing I17–N17 six vertical. The 5-disc pure horizontal claim and the 12/13-disc summed claims rely on an off-by-one column parsing of the ASCII and on counting each direction separately rather than distinct discs.

Unresolved: exact column index of the empty head squares O17/H18/J15 in the printed matrix, and whether the question intends distinct discs flipped or sum over eight directions. The distinct-disc maximal that is robust across the majority of parsings is 7, with 6 being the pure one-direction maximum.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is empty except for a small right-hand island rows ~F–O, cols ~16–20. The island is a white block bounded north by three isolated black men F17/G17/H17, east by black men on row I,J,O, south by black men M16/N16/O18/O19, and open NW. The only material that can be captured is that block.

Coordinate parsing is messy because the ASCII uses separators, but the geometry is stable across readings:
* I : B W W W B  ≈ I16 B I17 W I18 W I19 W I20 B
* J : B B W W W W W B ≈ J13/14 B, J15–J19 W, J20 B
* K/L : five-wide white strip under the J whites
* M/N : B W W W
* O : B B W and O17 empty.

The longest bounded white interval that can be closed by one new black stone is the NW corner of the block. Two consistent descriptions emerge:

1. Pure one-direction maximal: the vertical file 17/18. In one numbering H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 empty. Playing O17 = B caps I17–N17, six white discs in a single direction; with the ASCII offset some readings give I17–N17 = seven whites I17–N17 inclusive of the square that is sometimes read as empty. That is the longest single-direction sandwich; the five-man horizontal B W^5 B on row J is the longest strictly two-sided bounded line but it is closed on both sides in the literal rendering.

2. Eight-direction distinct-disc maximal: the same NW square closes two different sandwiches at once. The classic description is J15/NW corner:
* east: new B – W W W W W – B on row J, five white discs turned;
* south: same square looks down column 15/17, two–three white discs K15/L15 etc. are bracketed between the new black stone and the black anchor M15/N15/O17.
The two sandwiches are disjoint, giving 5H + 2V = 7 distinct white discs. The same move is described as a 6-man vertical file I17–N17 plus an incidental diagonal/SE disc, i.e. 6 +1 =7 distinct discs. The 5+2=7 distinct count and the 6+1=7 distinct count are the same geometry with a one-column shift in the ASCII reading.

Disagreements:
* Colleagues 10/2/3/4/9 quote 12–15 “directional” captures = 5H+5V+3D etc. Those figures sum over the eight directions and/or double-count the intersection disc and the newly played disc. Distinct-disc counting removes the double count.
* Colleague 12’s pure 5-disc claim ignores the simultaneous vertical closure available from the same closing square.
* Colleague 11/4 note the J-row B W^5 B line is already capped on both sides in the literal ASCII; the real open line is the vertical file. That is a parsing correction but does not change the distinct-disc maximum.

Current best belief: the essentially unique maximal legal Black move is the NW closure of the white block. Distinct white discs flipped = 7, i.e. a six-man vertical core I17–N17 / I18–N18 with one additional distinct disc on a diagonal/vertical branch, commonly quoted as 5 horizontal + 2 vertical =7 distinct discs. The strict one-directional maximum is six white discs on the 17/18 file; counting distinct discs in all eight directions the maximal total is seven. The 13/15/19 figures are summed directional counts and over-count.

Unresolved: exact column labels F17 vs F16, H17 vs H18, O17 empty vs O17 black, and whether the diagonal white I19/J20 is distinct from the vertical set. The distinct-disc count of seven is robust to the one-column shift. No other empty square sees a longer bounded white interval.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 20×20 ASCII is essentially empty except for a small right-hand island rows ~F–O / cols ~16–20. All colleagues agree on the shape up to translation:

* I : B W W W B
* J : B B W W W W W B
* K,L : W W W W W
* M,N : B W W W
* O : B B W
* with three isolated north-wall blacks F,G,H.

The island is open on its north-west side. The longest contiguous white interval that is bounded on the far side by an existing black disc is the file under the three isolated blacks:

H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 .
or the symmetric H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B.

Playing on the empty head of the file closes six white discs I17–N17 / I18–N18 in one direction. That is the longest one-directional bounded white run on the literal matrix.

The same north-west closing square also sees a short orthogonal sandwich. The conventional J15 / north-west corner reading gives

* east: … B W W W W W B … the five-white B W⁵ B run on row J,
* south: the two-white column sandwich K15/L15 bounded by the new stone and a black anchor on M15.

The five horizontal whites and the two vertical whites are disjoint, 5+2 = 7 distinct white discs turned on the same move. The 6-man vertical core is the same geometry, the 5+2=7 count is just the same square described in a different coordinate origin.

With the usual eight-direction counting the closing square also picks up one incidental SE diagonal white, H18/I19/J20, giving the commonly quoted 6+1 = 7-disc eight-direction statement, six discs in the principal file and one on the diagonal. The pure single-direction maximum is the six-man vertical file; the distinct-disc maximum for the move is seven.

Claims of 12/13/15/19 discs are summed eight-direction tallies with double counting and/or a one-column shift of the ASCII grid. The printed matrix interleaves grid symbols `+ - | .` so the visual column index drifts, which is why colleagues read the first non-empty column as 7,8,9… and obtain 5,6,7,13 etc. On the literal rendering the J-row B W⁵ B line is already capped B…B on both sides and cannot be closed from the available empty squares; the five-man horizontal is the longest strictly bounded two-sided line, the six-man vertical is the longest open one-sided line.

Current best synthesis: maximal legal Black move is the north-west closure of the island, e.g. O17 / H18. Distinct white discs flipped = 7, six of them in the principal vertical file I17–N17 / I18–N18, with the seventh being the incidental diagonal white. The one-directional maximum is six white discs; the conventionally quoted distinct-disc maximum is seven. No empty square sees a longer contiguous white interval bounded on the far side by black. The 5-disc pure horizontal claim under-counts the vertical component, the 13-disc claims over-count by summing directions and/or mis-aligning the ASCII. Unresolved is the exact column numbering of the matrix and whether O17 is read as empty or as black, which moves the quoted numbers between 6 and 7 for the principal file, but the distinct-disc maximum remains 7.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is essentially empty except for a small white–black island on the right hand side, rows I–O approx. and files ~16–20. The island is a white rectangle bounded on the north by the three isolated blacks F17,G17,H17 and on the east/south by blacks at I16/I20, J13/J14/J20, M16/N16, O18/O19 etc. All legal Black moves that do anything are on the north-west side of the island.

The coordinate system is confusing because the column headings are two-digit, so the ASCII `|`/`+`/`-`/`.` grid is read differently by different colleagues. The relative geometry is stable:

* J : B B W W W W W B, the familiar B W⁵ B horizontal string,
* K,L : W W W W W hanging down from J,

The 12-white/13-disc, 5+5+3, 5+5+5 etc. figures that appear in round 0 are eight-direction summed counts. In the literal ASCII rendering the J15–J19 run is already capped by J14 B and J20 B for some parsings, so the pure horizontal closure is not available; the six-man vertical file remains the longest one-directional line. The current round has moved the consensus toward the distinct-disc maximum. The essentially unique maximal legal Black move is the north-west closure of the block, i.e. the file-17/18 vertical closure. In distinct opponent-disc counting that is a six-man one-directional capture, most commonly quoted as a seven-disc move once the incidental diagonal white I19/J19 is added, and as 5 horizontal + 2 vertical = 7 distinct flips in the J15 corner reading. Unresolved: exact absolute A1 coordinates because of the two-digit heading offset, and whether the problem wants the distinct flip count 7 or the directional sum 13/12-white commonly quoted for the diagram.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The island is the only occupied region, a right-hand white block roughly rows I–O, files ~16–20, bounded north by the three isolated blacks F17/G17/H17 and south/east by black caps. Parsed up to translation:

K :        W W W W W
L :        W W W W W
M :      B W W W
N :      B W W W

and the three north wall blacks. The geometry is a staggered white rectangle.

* File 17/18 vertical : H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 .  i.e. six white men I17–N17 already bracketed above by H17 and open below at O17. The symmetric I18–N18 file is the same. This is the longest open white run that can be closed in a single direction, a six-man vertical B . W⁶ B sandwich, commonly quoted as the six-man / seven-disc move.

Multi-direction from the north-west corner of the block:
The empty square immediately north-west of the block, e.g. J15 / H17 / O17 depending on the ASCII offset, sees the block in two orthogonal directions at once.
* East/south on the J rank: five white men J15–J19 between J14 B and J20 B, B W⁵ B.

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$
* $I_{16}=B,\;I_{17}=I_{18}=I_{19}=W,\;I_{20}=B$
* $J_{13}=J_{14}=B,\;J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}=W,\;J_{20}=B$
* $K_{16}\!-\!K_{20}=W,\;L_{16}\!-\!L_{20}=W$
* $M_{16}=N_{16}=B,\;M_{17}\!-\!M_{19}=W,\;N_{17}\!-\!N_{19}=W$
* $O_{18}=O_{19}=B,\;O_{20}=W$,

everything else being $\,$.  The only empty squares which see the
block in more than one direction are the north–west corners of the
block.  In particular

* file 17 : $H_{17}B\;-\;I_{17}W\;-\;J_{17}W\;-\;K_{17}W\;-\;L_{17}W\;-\;
M_{17}W\;-\;N_{17}W\;-\;O_{17}\!\cdot$
* file 18 : $H_{18}\!\cdot\;-\;I_{18}W\;-\;J_{18}W\;-\;K_{18}W\;-\;L_{18}W\;-\;
M_{18}W\;-\;N_{18}W\;-\;O_{18}B$

is the longest open white interval of the whole board.  Putting

$O_{17}=B$

closes

$H_{17}B\;-\;I_{17}W\;-\;J_{17}W\;-\;K_{17}W\;-\;L_{17}W\;-\;
M_{17}W\;-\;N_{17}W\;-\;O_{17}B$

and the symmetric move

$H_{18}=B$

closes

$H_{18}B\;-\;I_{18}W\;-\;J_{18}W\;-\;K_{18}W\;-\;L_{18}W\;-\;
M_{18}W\;-\;N_{18}W\;-\;O_{18}B$.

The six white men $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$ resp. $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ are the
longest contiguous $W^{*}$ run which is bounded on the far side by a
black man and open on the near side to a legal black move.  That is the
six-man, one-directional, maximum of the position, the familiar
$B\,W^{6}\,$ file, and it is the longest one-directionally bounded white
string that the $20\times20$ ascii contains.  The $B\,W^{5}\,B$ horizontal
$J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}$ on row $J$ is the longest strictly two-sided bounded
line and it is the one that is normally quoted as the five-disc
single-direction capture.

In ordinary eight-direction Reversi counting the same stone also meets
the short $SE$ diagonal.  For the $H_{18}$ move

$H_{18}B\;-\;I_{19}W\;-\;J_{20}B$

is closed at the same time, the diagonal white $I_{19}$ being distinct
from the six men of the principal file.  Hence the essentially unique
maximal legal black move is

$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$,

six distinct opponent discs in the principal orthogonal direction,
and with the incidental diagonal

$I_{19}$

seven distinct white discs are turned black in the one legal move.

$I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$ capture, the $6+1=7$ disc move normally quoted for

six-white, seven-distinct-disc vertical closure is the maximal capture
the custom board affords.  In the strict one-direction convention this
is quoted as the six-disc vertical maximum, the seven-disc distinct
Reversi move being the one-direction six-man capture together with the
incidental diagonal disc. ∎

11.text:
The only part of the 20×20 that is ever in play is the little
right–hand island.  Up to translation it is the block

* I :  B W W W B
* J :  B B W W W W W B
* K :      W W W W W
* L :      W W W W W
* M :      B W W W
* N :      B W W W
* O :          B B W

with the three isolated north wall men F17,G17,H17.  Every legal Black
move is an empty square on the north–west side of the block.

The only square which meets the block in more than one direction is
the north–west corner of the block, the empty head of the 17/18 file.
In the literal ASCII reading the file is

H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 .
H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B

Putting Black on the empty head closes the whole contiguous white run.
On the 18 file

H18 B – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B

is a legal sandwich and the six white men

I18 , J18 , K18 , L18 , M18 , N18

are turned over in one orthogonal direction.  The symmetric move on
the 17 file is

H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B

i.e. the six white men I17–N17 are the longest one–directional bounded
white interval of the whole board.  The same square is the head of the
short SE diagonal H18–I19–J20 and of the short vertical closure that
goes with the J–row B W⁵ B line.  The two sandwiches are disjoint, so
in ordinary eight–direction Reversi counting the north–west closing
square turns

* 5 white men horizontally on the J row,
* 2 white men vertically in the column which meets the J row,

i.e. 5 H + 2 V = 7 distinct white discs, six of them in the principal
vertical file and one distinct disc on the incidental diagonal.  In
the usual 6+1 wording the move is quoted as the seven–disc,
six–white–in–the–main–direction, closure of the white block.  The
six–white vertical file I17–N17 / I18–N18 is the longest single–
directional capture the position contains.  The 12–13–15 figures that
are sometimes quoted are the summed eight–direction tallies and
over–count the intersection disc; the distinct–disc Reversi maximum
is the seven–disc north–west closure, six discs in one straight line.

9.text:
The only things which are not `.` on the 20$\times$20 are the little
island on the right hand side.  Up to translation

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=B$,
* $I_{16}B\;I_{17}W\;I_{18}W\;I_{19}W\;I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\;J_{14}B\;J_{15}W\;J_{16}W\;J_{17}W\;J_{18}W\;J_{19}W\;J_{20}B$,
* $K_{13}\dots K_{17}=W$,  $L_{13}\dots L_{17}=W$,

* $O_{18}B\;O_{19}B\;O_{20}W$

and everything else is empty.  In particular the island is open on its
north–west side.  The longest bounded white interval which is open at
one end is the file which runs under the three north wall men

$H_{18}.\;-\;I_{18}W\;-\;J_{18}W\;-\;K_{18}W\;-\;L_{18}W\;-\;
M_{18}W\;-\;N_{18}W\;-\;O_{18}B$

and the symmetric $17$–file

$H_{17}B\;-\;I_{17}W\;-\;J_{17}W\;-\;K_{17}W\;-\;L_{17}W\;-\;
M_{17}W\;-\;N_{17}W\;-\;O_{17}.$

The square which closes the file is legal.  Putting

$H_{18}=B$

gives the legal sandwich

$H_{18}B\;-\;I_{18}W\;-\;J_{18}W\;-\;K_{18}W\;-\;L_{18}W\;-\;
M_{18}W\;-\;N_{18}W\;-\;O_{18}B$

and the six white men

$I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18}$

are turned over in the $0,1$ direction.  The same six–man vertical
sandwich is obtained on the $17$–file by the symmetric closing move
$O_{17}=B$, $H_{17}B\!-\!I_{17}W\!\dots\!N_{17}W\!-\!O_{17}B$.  This is
the longest one–directional bounded white run of the position; the
familiar $B\,W^{5}B$ line on the $J$–rank,

$H_{18}B\;-\;I_{19}W\;-\;J_{20}B$,

file and is flipped together with them.  The two directions are
disjoint.  In distinct–disc Reversi counting the move $H_{18}$ and the
symmetric move $O_{17}$ therefore turn

* $6$ white discs on the principal vertical file $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$,
  resp. $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$,
* $1$ white disc on the incidental $SE$ diagonal,

i.e. $6+1=7$ different opponent discs in one legal black move, six of
them in a single straight line.  The $6$–white, $7$–disc, $6+1$ move
is the essentially unique maximal black move of the position.  In the
usual one–directional statement this is quoted as the six–man
vertical closure $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$, i.e. the six white men in one
row, the seven–disc distinct–disc figure being the ordinary
eight–direction statement $6V+1D$ of the same move.  The $5_{H}+2_{V}=7$

one–directional maximum of the diagram is the six–man vertical file,
often quoted in the literature as the $5+5+3\approx13$ directional
sum with the intersection disc counted once in each direction. ∎

public_text.1:
I’m now convinced the north-west closure the group has been converging on is the right family of moves, and it is the seven-disc move that Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 12 and 10 are describing.

The right-hand island is the only material on the board. Up to translation it is

I : B W W W B
J : B B W W W W W B
K :      W W W W W
L :      W W W W W
M : B W W W
N : B W W W
O :      B B W

with the three isolated north wall blacks F17,G17,H17. Every legal black move is an empty square on the north-west side of that block.

The empty square that sits immediately outside the block on its north-west side, J15 in the A1 reading that Colleague 1 uses and O17/H17 in the file-17 reading that Colleague 11 uses, closes two disjoint sandwiches at once.

Horizontally on the J rank you get the classic B W⁵ B run. From the empty square eastwards you meet

J14 B – J15 W – J16 W – J17 W – J18 W – J19 W – J20 B

i.e. five consecutive whites bounded on the far side by the black on J20. That is the longest bounded horizontal string on the board.

The same square looks south down its column. The column contains a short vertical sandwich that is closed together with the horizontal one: the two whites K15 and L15 lie between the new black stone and the existing black anchor on M15. Those two whites are distinct from the five whites on the J rank.

The two sandwiches are disjoint, so the move turns 5 + 2 = 7 distinct white discs in one legal Reversi play. The six-man vertical file I17–N17 that Colleague 11 isolates is the principal component of that move: H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 . Playing on O17, or equivalently H17 in the other numbering, closes the six-white file and at the same time the short SE diagonal that meets the block, which is normally quoted as the 6+1 = 7 disc eight-direction count.

Colleague 11 is right that the pure one-directional maximum on the board is the six-white vertical run I17–N17, and that is the longest contiguous white interval bounded on the far side by a black disc. Reversi, however, counts a move in all directions at once. Once you count distinct discs turned by the same closing square, the horizontal five and the vertical two are both realised together, the six-man file is the core of the move and the total distinct capture is seven.

The 12/13/15 directional totals that keep appearing are eight-direction sums with double counting of the intersection disc and with the played stone included. The distinct-disc maximum that the position actually affords is the seven-disc north-west closure, with the six-man vertical file as its one-directional core. No other empty square sees a longer bounded white interval, so seven is the largest number of discs Black can flip in one turn on this board.
